descriptors.definition: A compromise involves a mutual settlement of an existing dispute through concessions by parties, whereas an arrangement modifies rights without a necessary dispute. Reconstruction alters and reorganizes a single company's capital or structure, while amalgamation blends two or more entities into one.
inclusion: Debt waiver and debt-to-equity conversions
Reduction of share capital
Mergers and demergers of undertakings
exclusion: Standard operational asset sales outside a restructuring scheme
Ordinary course of business debt settlements
nearby_distinctions: Compromise requires a dispute unlike an arrangement
Reconstruction applies to a single entity unlike amalgamation involving multiple entities

descriptors.concept_name: Power To Compromise Or Make Arrangements With Creditors And Members [Section 230]
descriptors.definition: The Tribunal is empowered to order and direct meetings of creditors, members, or classes thereof upon receiving an application from eligible stakeholders. Eligible applicants include the company, creditors, members, or a liquidator in cases of voluntary liquidation.
inclusion: Applications by company or liquidators
Meetings of specific classes of members or creditors
Consolidation and division of share classes
exclusion: Direct corporate actions executed without Tribunal meeting orders where statutory paths differ
nearby_distinctions: Differs from Section 232 merger approvals by focusing on initial meeting ordering and basic compromise frameworks

descriptors.concept_name: Power Of Tribunal To Enforce Compromise Or Arrangement [Section 231]
descriptors.definition: The Tribunal possesses supervisory authority over the implementation of sanctioned compromises and can issue directions or modifications. If a scheme cannot be satisfactorily implemented and the company is unable to pay its debts, the Tribunal may order a winding up.
inclusion: Supervising scheme execution
Issuing necessary implementation directions
Directing company winding up due to implementation failure
exclusion: Initial ordering of meetings under Section 230
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on post-sanction enforcement and supervision rather than initial scheme formulation

descriptors.definition: The Tribunal may order meetings and sanction schemes involving corporate reconstruction, mergers, or the transfer of undertakings between companies. Merging companies must circulate specific disclosures, including director reports, valuation reports, and share exchange ratios, prior to such meetings.
inclusion: Reconstruction schemes involving mergers
Transfer of property or liabilities to one or more companies
Circulation of expert valuation and director explanation reports
exclusion: Stand-alone debt compromises without structural amalgamation elements
nearby_distinctions: Specifically governs structural mergers and undertakings transfers leveraging Section 230 meeting procedures

descriptors.concept_name: Power To Acquire Shares Of Shareholders Dissenting From Scheme Or Contract Approved By Majority [Section 235]
descriptors.definition: A transferee company can acquire shares of dissenting minority shareholders when a share transfer scheme is approved by holders of at least nine-tenths in value within four months. The acquiring company must issue a notice within two months after that period to buy out the remaining shares.
instrument_references: Rule 26 of Companies (Compromises, Arrangements and Amalgamations) Rules, 2016
inclusion: Compulsory acquisition of dissenting shares upon high-threshold majority approval
Tribunal applications by dissenting shareholders objecting to acquisition notices
exclusion: Shares already held by the transferee company or its subsidiaries at the offer date
nearby_distinctions: Applies specifically to contractual share transfer schemes approved by 90 percent majority rather than general demergers

descriptors.definition: An acquirer or group holding ninety percent or more of a company's equity share capital must notify their intention to buy out remaining shares from minority shareholders. Both majorities and minorities can trigger buyouts at a price determined by a registered valuer.
instrument_references: Rule 27 of Companies (Compromises, Arrangements and Amalgamations) Rules, 2016
inclusion: Mandatory notifications by ninety percent holders
Valuation-based minority share purchases
Deposit of acquisition amounts in separate bank accounts
exclusion: Acquisitions falling below the statutory ninety percent threshold
nearby_distinctions: Triggered automatically upon reaching a ninety percent holding threshold via any route, unlike Section 235 scheme approvals

descriptors.concept_name: Power Of Central Government To Provide For Amalgamation Of Companies In Public Interest [Section 237]
descriptors.definition: The Central Government may order the amalgamation of companies in the public interest by notification in the Official Gazette. Affected members and creditors are entitled to equivalent rights in the transferee entity or compensation if their interests are diminished.
inclusion: Government-mandated public interest amalgamations
Continuation of pending legal proceedings
Compensation rights for diminished member or creditor interests
exclusion: Voluntary company-driven schemes processed via the Tribunal
nearby_distinctions: Executed directly by the Central Government based on public interest rather than through standard Tribunal petition processes

descriptors.concept_name: Registration Of Offer Of Schemes Involving Transfer Of Shares [Section 238]
descriptors.definition: Circulars containing share transfer offers and board recommendations under Section 235 must be presented to the Registrar for registration with mandatory cash availability disclosures. Issuing unregistered circulars attracts personal financial penalties for responsible directors.
instrument_references: Rule 28 of Companies (Compromises, Arrangements and Amalgamations) Rules, 2016
inclusion: Mandatory registration of offer circulars with the Registrar
Cash availability disclosures by the transferee company
Appeals to the Tribunal against Registrar refusal
exclusion: Internal corporate communications unrelated to share transfer scheme offers
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on administrative pre-requisites and registration of offer documentation rather than substantive scheme sanctioning

descriptors.concept_name: Preservation Of Books And Papers Of Amalgamated Companies [Section 239]
descriptors.definition: Books and papers of companies involved in amalgamations or share acquisitions cannot be disposed of without prior Central Government permission. The Central Government may inspect these documents to uncover evidence of offences related to formation or management.
inclusion: Restriction on document disposal without government consent
Appointment of examiners to investigate historical corporate records
exclusion: Routine destruction of operational documents outside the scope of statutory amalgamations or acquisitions
nearby_distinctions: Applies specifically to records of amalgamated or acquired entities to preserve legal accountability

descriptors.concept_name: Liability Of Officers In Respect Of Offences Committed Prior To Merger, Amalgamation, Etc. [Section 240]
descriptors.definition: Officers in default remain personally liable for offences committed under the Act prior to a company's merger, amalgamation, or acquisition. This liability survives despite structural corporate changes and overrides other conflicting laws.
inclusion: Continuation of statutory penalties and liabilities for past default offences after restructuring
exclusion: Absolution of officer accountability resulting from structural corporate blending
nearby_distinctions: Targets individual officer liability rather than corporate entity liabilities

descriptors.concept_name: Fast Track Mode Of Merger Or Amalgamation Of Certain Companies [Section 233]
descriptors.definition: Specific entities like small companies, start-ups, and holding-subsidiary pairs can execute mergers through an expedited administrative process without Tribunal petitions. The scheme requires creditor and member approvals, declarations of solvency, and confirmation from the Regional Director.
instrument_references: Rule 25 of Companies (Compromises, Arrangements and Amalgamations) Rules, 2016
inclusion: Mergers between small companies or start-ups
Holding and wholly-owned subsidiary amalgamations
Regional Director confirmation procedures
exclusion: Standard corporate mergers involving large non-qualifying public companies requiring NCLT adjudication
nearby_distinctions: Operates via regional administrative clearance rather than traditional NCLT petition mechanisms

descriptors.definition: Indian companies and foreign bodies corporate can engage in cross-border mergers subject to prior regulatory approvals and specific statutory rules. Foreign companies may merge into Indian entities, and Indian entities can merge into foreign counterparts located in permitted jurisdictions.
instrument_references: Rule 25A of Companies (Compromises, Arrangements and Amalgamations) Rules, 2016
inclusion: Inbound mergers of foreign companies into Indian companies
Outbound mergers of Indian companies into foreign jurisdictions
Consideration paid in cash or Depository Receipts
exclusion: Stand-alone cross-border demergers or compromises not classified as structural mergers
nearby_distinctions: Governs international corporate combinations involving foreign jurisdictions rather than purely domestic reorganizations
